answer: To counter Sybil attacks, an agent economy can use trust-graph random walks. Honest nodes form authenticated peer edges, restricting discovery to paths traversing a verified network inlet. An adversary cannot rely on a synthetic echo among colluding bots, but must incur the scarce cost of cultivating genuine, sustained transaction histories with honest peers per identity. However, honest newcomers suffer severe cold-start friction, and decentralized graph convergence advances like a glacier.
